A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of Improved Training Technique for Latent Consistency Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and four-page Appendix A support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original latent-space analyses, image-generation evaluations and ablations in Sections 4–5 and Tables 1–2, with generated samples in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative evaluations, ablations and generated samples, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same Cauchy loss, low-noise diffusion regularizer, minibatch OT coupling, adaptive scaling-c schedule and Non-scaling LayerNorm. Removing the OT illustration does not change the procedure described in Section 4.4.

E1.justification: Both evaluate generation on CelebA-HQ, LSUN Church and FFHQ at 256×256, and use CIFAR-10 in the pixel-versus-latent analysis. The appendix retains the same datasets and sampling scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same comparators within each experiment. RDUOT's reference changes title and year, but its baseline row and scores remain unchanged; the new introductory citations are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The VAE preprocessing, VE forward process, architectures, one- and two-step sampling, 50K-image FID/Recall evaluation and listed training budgets remain unchanged. CelebA-HQ ablations still use 1,400 training epochs.

E4.justification: Both retain the component, robust-loss, diffusion-threshold, normalization and scaling-schedule analyses, including the appendix loss-comparison samples. The removed OT diagram illustrates coupling rather than supplying a separate ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The descriptive boxplots of data and temporal differences are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical entries; for example, Table 1's proposed-method one-step FIDs remain 7.27, 8.87 and 8.72 for CelebA-HQ, LSUN Church and FFHQ. The convergence curves, main-text samples and all eight appendix image grids are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same consistency formulations, losses, schedules and normalization definitions. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: addressing latent-space outliers and improving one- or two-step consistency generation to narrow the gap with diffusion models.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting outliers, loss robustness, OT and normalization to training behavior remain intact. v2 trims repeated conclusions without changing their meaning, and retains the comparison caveats about different forward processes and the same future directions.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same VAE checkpoint, UNet architecture, POT implementation, schedule parameters and approximately 0.93% OT training overhead. The implementation link and technical access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Han et al. (2024), ProxEdit, and Zhangli et al. (2024), Layout-agnostic scene text image synthesis with diffusion models, to the introductory application examples and references. The positioning relative to consistency training and distillation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates Khanh Doan's affiliation, adds funding acknowledgements, shortens several repetitive sentences and simplifies some terminology and cross-references. The section sequence and scientific narrative remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 removes v1 Figure 3's OT illustration, reduces several plot sizes, enlarges the main qualitative sample panels and relocates Table 2 vertically as the text reflows. Subsequent figures are renumbered; the appendix displays retain the same images and arrangement.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the method, mathematical content, quantitative results and appendix evidence. Added background citations and light editing provide limited benefits, while deleting the OT schematic and shrinking plots reduce some visual explanation. These modest presentation tradeoffs do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
